Great Synagogue in Rome

Synagogue · Lazio, Italy

The Tempio Maggiore di Roma (Great Synagogue of Rome) is the main synagogue of Rome and one of the city’s most important symbols of Jewish life. Inaugurated in 1904, it was built after the emancipation of Rome’s Jewish community and the end of the centuries-old Ghetto. Designed by Vincenzo Costa and Osvaldo Armanni, the monumental building combines classical forms with Assyrian-Babylonian influences and is crowned by a distinctive square aluminum-covered dome visible across the Roman skyline.

The richly decorated synagogue remains an active place of worship and a central institution of Rome’s historic Jewish community. The same monumental complex also houses the Jewish Museum of Rome, which presents the history, traditions, and heritage of one of the world’s oldest continuous Jewish communities.
